summary.headline: Indoco Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7.4% to Rs 5,069 mn, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.2% from 12.4% on freight and material costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue crossed Rs 500 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 7.4% YoY to Rs 5,069 mn, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 464 mn at 9.2% margin. Standalone revenue grew only 2% to Rs 4,381 mn, with standalone EBITDA margin down to 9.2% from 12.4%. Management attributed the margin pressure to roughly Rs 13 crore of extra freight and higher material, solvent and handling costs linked to the geopolitical conflict. Domestic formulations declined to Rs 2,128 mn from Rs 2,261 mn as seasonal acute brands (Febrex Plus, Oxipod, ATL) degrew sharply, while the regulated international markets grew 21.1%.

financial_highlights.metric: AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions revenue

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue fell to Rs 2,128 mn from Rs 2,261 mn. Cyclopam crossed Rs 200 crore (Rs 206 crore sales) and Cital and dental portfolio grew about 30%, but Febrex Plus, Oxipod and ATL degrew by a similar value.

segments.name: Regulated international markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 21.1% to Rs 1,109 mn: Europe up 23.5% to Rs 675 mn, US up 16.4% to Rs 391 mn, South Africa/Australia/NZ up 31.2% to Rs 43 mn.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 612 mn was broadly flat against Rs 618 mn. Roughly Rs 10 crore of Africa ophthal sales were divested, and management expects Rs 10-12 crore of impact to remain this year.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 4.6% to Rs 451 mn. Management said the business shows resilience and is strategically important for supply security.

segments.name: AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20.8% to Rs 82 mn from Rs 68 mn.

segments.name: Warren Remedies (toothpaste/OTC)
segments.commentary: Toothpaste division revenue was about Rs 36 crore in the quarter and is near breakeven after reduced advertising; about Rs 16 crore was spent on promotion in H1. Warren API is mostly internal consumption with no approvals yet.

guidance_outlook: Domestic formulations: high single-digit FY27 growth reiterated, with more predictable sales expected in H2; management said it would not revise guidance.
Emerging markets: expected to return to good double-digit growth, with Q4 typically strong; H1 growth about 8%.
Regulated markets: management targets 20%+ growth in Europe and UK over the next 1-2 years.
R&D expected to stay below 5% of topline; YTD at about 4%.
Capex to stay at bare minimum; no major capex expected in H2 FY27 or FY28.
FY27 debt repayment target reaffirmed; H1 repayment about Rs 65 crore at consolidated level.
Management said freight cost impact duration is uncertain, with consolidated other expenses slightly above the roughly Rs 150-160 crore guided range.
capex_capacity: Capex in H1 per cash flow was about Rs 60 crore, but management said actual PPE capex (land etc.) is under Rs 25 crore; the balance is capitalised intangibles (ANDA and dossier R&D). Company agreed to bifurcate disclosure between PPE and other intangibles.
Warren Remedies: recent API site and finished product site capex has been completed.
Warren API US FDA audit expected by Q2 next year; CEPs approved and DMFs filed.
Plant-1 Goa received a successful MHRA audit and ANVISA clearance for the RCRO AnaCipher.
Goa plant USFDA inspection received 7 observations; response submitted, with outcome expected by first week of December.
Management said the company can add shifts across plants if needed and can reach roughly 4X current international topline with existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Freight and material cost pressure: management cited around Rs 13 crore of additional freight impact in the quarter and COGS, RMPM, freight and handling costs up roughly 30%, weighing on gross margin.

Domestic weakness was attributed to an almost absent monsoon hitting seasonal acute and anti-infective/anti-cold categories; anti-infectives and respiratory were about 30% of domestic business, down from over 50% earlier.
Cyclopam prescriptions grew about 16%; Cyclopam, Cital and dental portfolio grew about 30%, while Febrex Plus was down about 20% and ATM down about 16%.
About Rs 100 crore MAT sales come from products launched in the last two years.
FPP (US) turned profitable in H1 with H1 revenue above Rs 100 crore; management flagged US generic price erosion and competition.
LATAM grew 57%; French West Africa growing at higher double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other and employee expenses rise this quarter despite earlier cost reduction and headcount cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to about Rs 13 crore of freight cost, mainly in international business; employee costs fell a couple of percentage points as a share of sales, and consolidated expenses were slightly above the roughly Rs 160 crore guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic guidance be maintained and what drives H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated high single-digit growth for FY27, citing about Rs 65 crore Ophthal base impact and expecting more predictable H2 sales; it said weak rains hurt the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What explains H1 capex of about Rs 60 crore against guidance of about Rs 40 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the difference is capitalised intangibles from ANDA and dossier R&D; actual PPE capex is under Rs 25 crore, and no major capex is planned for H2 or next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a new subsidiary (Warren Life Sciences) registered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the OTC toothpaste and API businesses are very different and separate tracking is needed; it registered Warren Life Sciences with the intent of possibly separating the two businesses, not for funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US FDA outcome expectation for the Goa plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said responses have been submitted, with data updates sent to USFDA, and the company expects to know the outcome by the first week of December; none of the seven observations relate to data integrity or cleaning validation.

qa_highlights.question: Can Europe and UK regulated markets grow 20%+ for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that is the target, citing steady order positions and good offtake in Europe and UK.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin pressure from freight and raw material costs; duration of the geopolitical-driven cost increase is uncertain.
Domestic franchise: high single-digit FY27 guidance depends on H2 recovery in seasonal acute brands after a weak monsoon.
USFDA Goa plant response outcome expected by early December with seven observations.
Warren Remedies toothpaste losses and ad spend; API unit under-utilised with no approvals yet; Warren API US FDA audit targeted for Q2 next year.
Operating cash flow conversion weak: H1 OCF about Rs 50 crore against EBITDA of about Rs 80 crore (about 60-65%), versus 75-90% historically.
Emerging markets flat in H1 with Ophthal divestment impact of Rs 10-12 crore this year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on international and regulated markets and on the FDA outcome, but defensive on domestic performance and margins. Management repeatedly blamed weather, freight and the Ophthal divestment, and declined to quantify several items (GC margins, launches, MMP savings, FPP breakeven).
key_quotes: Cyclopam has further strengthened its position as a flagship brand, crossing the Rs. 200 crore threshold and now at a sales of Rs. 206 crore and maintaining its number two position in the antispasmodics and anticholinergics market.

growth.why: Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 domestic growth and 20%+ Europe/UK growth targets, backed by Cyclopam, Cital and dental growth and regulated markets up 21.1%, but gave no specific new capacity; capex is at bare minimum with no major spend in H2 or FY28, and the domestic guidance faces a weak seasonal-acute base.
